A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GRIFFIN and provide readable text, equations, figures, and tables sufficient for comparison. v1 has no appendix; v2's Appendices A–F were included in the assessment.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original decoding experiments and component ablations, including Table 1, Tables 2–5, and Figure 5.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendices A–B report original decoding experiments, retained ablations, and additional architectural and expansion-width results.

M1.justification: The TAT/TGF/TEH framework is retained, but the stated TGF expansion changes from 3d to 4d, and Equation 3 revises mask propagation to include the current token's temporary mask. These are limited changes to the reported method specification. Appendix A.3 separately specifies an FFN-sized expansion of 11,008, leaving the implemented width change unclear.

E1.justification: Both versions train on ShareGPT and evaluate MT-Bench dialogue, HumanEval code generation, and GSM8K mathematical reasoning. The additional target models in v2 expand model configurations within the same dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 substantially prunes comparisons within retained model settings. Hydra disappears; EAGLE remains only for LLaMA3-8B; PLD and Lookahead remain only for LLaMA2-7B; and Medusa is removed for LLaMA3-8B. EAGLE-2, FSPAD, and HASS remain across the original model comparisons.

E3.justification: v2 adds evaluations using Qwen2-7B, LLaMA3-70B, and Mixtral-8x7B, with two A100 GPUs for the latter two instead of the original single-GPU setting. It also adds expansion-width controls and speedup measurements to the ablations. The original benchmarks, batch size 1, and temperatures 0 and 1 remain.

E4.justification: Appendices A.2–A.3 add tests removing fusion subcomponents and varying expansion width, addressing architectural necessity and capacity-versus-speed tradeoffs. Existing ablations gain speedup results. The direct TGF/TEH misalignment-rate ablation in v1 Figure 5 is removed, while v2 Table 8 evaluates those components through acceptance length and speedup.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Results remain point estimates; additional rows do not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds three target-model result groups, ablation speedups, and architectural/width results, while revising numerous baseline scores and Figure 1 values. GRIFFIN's original per-dataset Table 1 scores remain unchanged, but its LLaMA2-7B mean speedup at temperature 1 is corrected from 3.17 to 3.07. These changes do not establish a same-setting improvement in GRIFFIN itself.

T1.justification: Equation 3 changes the mathematical mask definition from a product of preceding masks through t−1 to temporary masks including t. v2 also omits v1's explicit averaged multi-pass objective. The added TGF equations largely formalize existing architectural prose; no theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central token-alignment contribution remains. v2 explicitly claims to be the first to expose and address token misalignment, extends its empirical claims to Qwen and Mixtral, and revises the abstract's acceptance-length/speedup improvements from over 7%/8% to over 8%/7%.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations involving Qwen's vocabulary and LM-head cost, MoE verification overhead, and expansion-width tradeoffs. Appendices E–F discuss larger draft models and quantify higher training costs than HASS, qualifying the largely retained main-text argument about comparable training overhead.

D1.justification: Appendices C–F replace sparse implementation documentation with draft-tree settings, optimizer and training hyperparameters, baseline checkpoint/training provenance, parameter counts, and GPU-hour estimates. v2 also adds code and draft-model release information. These disclosures do not establish that retained experiments changed their settings.

R1.justification: v2 adds the Qwen technical report and Mixtral of Experts references and strengthens its priority claim concerning token misalignment. The related-work coverage and positioning against EAGLE, HASS, FSPAD, and other speculative-decoding approaches otherwise remain substantially similar.

P1.justification: Substantial passages in the introduction, motivation, method explanation, and ablation discussion are rewritten. Experimental setup is folded into Section 5, and supporting analyses and implementation material are organized into Appendices A–F. The changes extend well beyond local copyediting.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column presentation. Architecture diagrams are redrawn, v1 Figures 3–4 are merged into v2 Figure 3, and v1 Figure 5 is removed. Tables 1–5 are restructured or expanded, and Tables 6–8 are added.

improvement.justification: The added architectural controls, broader model evaluations, and detailed reproducibility information strengthen v2 relative to v1. The net gain is limited by reduced baseline coverage and unresolved inconsistencies: Section 5.1's 8.7% MT-Bench gain at temperature 0 disagrees with Table 1's 3.09 versus 2.75, and the retained same-training-cost claim conflicts with Appendix F's higher GRIFFIN costs.
